title: Profit, loss and percentage change
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:56Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point teaches finding a percentage of an amount and applying an increase or discount, but not calculating profit or loss from cost and selling prices or finding a percentage change by dividing the change by the original amount, so it is a related idea rather than the same one.

draft.title: Profit, loss and percentage change
card: Profit = selling price − cost price. It is a profit when the selling price is higher than the cost price.
Loss = cost price − selling price. It is a loss when the selling price is lower than the cost price.
Percentage change = change ÷ original amount × 100. The original amount is the one you started with, which for profit and loss is the cost price.
Example: Zoe buys a bike for $200 and sells it for $250. Profit = 250 − 200 = $50. Percentage profit = 50 ÷ 200 × 100 = 25%.
draft.remember: Find the change first, then divide by the original amount and times 100.

a.q: Sam buys a skateboard for $80 and sells it for $100. What is the profit?
a.why: Profit = selling price − cost price = 100 − 80 = $20. The value $180 comes from adding the two prices instead of subtracting.
a.clue: Subtract the cost price from the selling price.

b.q: Leah buys a lamp for $50 and sells it for $40. What is her percentage loss?
b.why: The loss is 50 − 40 = $10. Percentage loss = 10 ÷ 50 × 100 = 20%. Dividing by the selling price gives 25%, which is wrong because the change is divided by the original cost price.
b.clue: Divide the loss by the amount you started with.

final.title: Profit, loss and percentage change
card: Profit \(=\) selling price \(-\) cost price. It is a profit when the selling price is higher than the cost price.

Example: Zoe buys a bike for $200 and sells it for $250. Profit \(= 250 - 200 = \$50\). Percentage profit \(= 50 \div 200 \times 100 = 25\%\).
